skill.name: ponytail-review
skill.description: Reviews code diffs for unnecessary complexity and reports concise deletion or simplification opportunities with concrete replacements.
skill.summary: Find removable complexity and simpler native alternatives in code diffs.
skill.author: dietrichgebert

security_audit.summary: All 14 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code used for labels, output formats, and examples. SKILL.md contains no executable commands, prompt injection, or other semantic security concerns.

static_findings.snippet: - `delete:` dead code, unused flexibility, speculative feature. Replacement: nothing.
- `stdlib:` hand-rolled thing the standard library ships. Name the function.
- `native:` dependency or code doing what the platform already does. Name the feature.
- `yagni:` abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets, layer with one caller.
- `shrink:` same logic, fewer lines. Show the shorter form.

content.value_statement: Complex diffs can hide unnecessary abstractions, dependencies, and dead flexibility. This skill produces concise, location-specific suggestions for deletion or simpler replacements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews diffs for dead code, unused flexibility, and speculative features.
Identifies hand-built utilities that standard library functions can replace.
Flags dependencies used for features already provided by the platform.
Finds abstractions with one implementation or configuration nobody uses.
Suggests shorter equivalent forms and estimates potential net line reduction.
Returns location-tagged, one-line findings without modifying files.
limitations: Reviews unnecessary complexity only, not correctness, security, or performance.
Does not apply changes or verify behavior after suggested deletions.
Requires a readable code diff with useful file and line context.
Line reduction estimates are advisory and may need human validation.

use_cases.title: Simplify Before Merge
use_cases.description: Review a feature diff for removable layers, unused options, and shorter standard alternatives before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Focus Pull Request Feedback
use_cases.description: Produce concise complexity findings that complement a separate correctness and security review.

use_cases.title: Reduce Maintenance Cost
use_cases.description: Evaluate refactoring diffs for abstractions and dependencies that increase long-term maintenance without current value.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Simplicity Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff for over-engineering. List each removable or shrinkable element with its location and replacement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a small, focused change.

prompt_templates.title: Dependency and Standard Library Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff for dependencies and custom utilities that native platform or standard library features can replace.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a change adds packages or helper functions.

prompt_templates.title: Abstraction Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Find single-use abstractions, speculative configuration, and unused flexibility in this diff. Suggest direct replacements and estimate removed lines.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for service layers, factories, interfaces, or configuration changes.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-File Reduction Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-file diff only for unnecessary complexity. Prioritize safe deletions, native replacements, and shorter equivalent logic by potential line reduction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a large refactor after separate correctness and security reviews.

output_examples.input: A diff adds a repository interface with one implementation and one caller.
output_examples.output: repository.py:L18-44: yagni: Single-use repository abstraction. Inline it until a second implementation exists.

output_examples.input: A diff adds a date library for one localized formatting call.
output_examples.output: profile.ts:L7: native: Date library used once. Replace it with the platform date formatter and remove the dependency.

output_examples.input: A small diff is already direct and contains no removable complexity.

best_practices: Provide the complete diff with file names and line numbers.
Run correctness and security reviews separately before accepting deletion suggestions.
Validate behavior with focused tests after applying any recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as the only review for production code.
Do not remove abstractions that already support multiple real implementations.
Do not treat estimated line reduction as proof that a change is safer.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews code diffs for unnecessary complexity, removable code, avoidable dependencies, and speculative abstractions.

faq.question: Does it find correctness bugs?
faq.answer: No. Correctness, security, and performance require separate review passes.

faq.question: Will it modify my files?
faq.answer: No. It only reports concise findings and suggested replacements.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Provide a focused diff with file names, line numbers, and enough surrounding context to understand each change.

faq.question: How are findings formatted?
faq.answer: Each finding includes a location, a category tag, the removable complexity, and a replacement.

faq.question: What happens when the diff is already simple?
faq.answer: The skill returns a short confirmation and does not invent findings.
